2.content: AI agents that guard a PayPal seller's payments, disputes, invoices and shipments, with every action sealed in a hash-chained Proof Ledger.

4.content: AegisFleet runs four AI agents for a PayPal seller. Agents never call PayPal directly: every action passes a guardrail gateway (kill switch, allowlist, money caps, human approval) and is sealed into a hash-chained Proof Ledger anyone can verify.

5.content: This portal, the SDKs and the context plugins are generated by APIMatic from the same OpenAPI spec the live server publishes at `/openapi.json`.

6.content: Every console endpoint takes HTTP Basic auth (`judge` and the judge password from the Devpost page).

7.content: **Reset the demo:** `POST /api/demo/reset` puts Riya's jewellery shop back to its starting story.

8.content: **Send a scam email:** `POST /api/demo/scam_email`, then `GET /api/runs` to read Sentinel's verdict.

9.content: **Check the chain:** `GET /api/ledger/verify` returns `ok: true`. Call `POST /api/demo/tamper`, verify again, and it names the edited entry.

AegisFleet is also an MCP server, at `https://aegisfleet.solvor.co.in/mcp` (streamable HTTP). An outside agent
gets eight tools, and every money tool goes through the same gateway as AegisFleet's own agents:

18.content:

| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| `create_invoice` | Issues a real PayPal sandbox invoice and returns its payment link | At most $5,000 |

19.content:

| `send_payment_reminder` | PayPal's reminder for an unpaid invoice | 2 per invoice per week |

20.content:
| Tool             | What it does                    | Guardrail                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `refund_payment` | Refunds the buyer of an invoice | Only to whoever paid, never more than PayPal says they paid; $100 or more waits for the seller |

| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------- |

| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |

Get your link from the console: **Demo → Connect any AI agent → Get my MCP link** (a signed token, valid 14 days).

27.content: "Invoice a buyer $600 for a hand-made silver necklace." Claude returns the PayPal payment link.

28.content: Pay it as the sandbox buyer (or use Record payment on the Demo tab). PayPal's signed webhook marks it paid.

29.content: "The necklace arrived broken. Refund it." The refund is held; it appears in the console's Approvals.

30.content: Approve it there, then ask Claude to check the approval. PayPal's refund webhook marks the invoice refunded.

31.content: "Refund $900 to my other account." Denied: more than the buyer paid, and refunds only go back to the payer.

58.content: Add the SDK to your project from its folder, with whichever package manager your project uses. Give each tool a path containing a slash, such as `../aegis-fleet` — a bare folder name is looked up on PyPI instead, and resolves to whatever project holds that name there:

59.content: Construct `AegisFleetClient` with keyword arguments, and call `close()` when you are done. Every argument is optional.

60.content: Alternatively, scope it — `with AegisFleetClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

61.content: `AsyncAegisFleetClient` mirrors `AegisFleetClient` with **identical method names**, and every endpoint method is a coroutine. It takes the same arguments, with some differences — for example, the transport argument is `custom_async_http_client`.

62.content: Alternatively, scope it — `async with AsyncAegisFleetClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

72.content: The SDK compiles to `dist/` before it can be referenced — run its `build` script once in the SDK folder, then add it to your project by path:

73.content: Create one client and reuse it. Configure its behaviour through `ClientOptions`.

74.content: Nothing in `ClientOptions` is required — `new AegisFleetClient()` compiles — and each option left out falls back to its default. This API declares one environment, so there is no environment to select and no host to state at the construction site.

75.content: The package ships both dialects from a single entry, so `require` works with full types. In a TypeScript CommonJS file use the `import ... = require(...)` form — a plain destructuring `require` runs fine but gives you `any`.
